description.en: A short sample e-book on Indian Geography — physical divisions, rivers, climate and monsoon. Full chapter content will be added soon.
description.as: ভাৰতীয় ভূগোলৰ ওপৰত এটা চমু নমুনা ই-বুক — ভূ-বিভাগ, নদী, জলবায়ু আৰু মৌচুমী। সম্পূৰ্ণ অধ্যায়ৰ বিষয়বস্তু অচিৰেই যোগ হ'ব।

content.en:
India is divided into five major physical divisions. In the north lie the Himalayan mountains, which contain the highest peaks of the world. Below them stretch the great northern plains formed by the Indus, the Ganga and the Brahmaputra river systems.

The Peninsular plateau of the south is an ancient landmass, bounded by the Aravallis in the north-west and divided into the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau by the Vindhya and Satpura ranges. The plateau is flanked by the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats. Around the peninsula lie the coastal plains and two groups of islands — the Andaman and Nicobar islands in the Bay of Bengal and the Lakshadweep islands in the Arabian Sea.

The rivers of India are grouped into Himalayan rivers and Peninsular rivers. The Himalayan rivers such as the Ganga, the Indus and the Brahmaputra are perennial and flow throughout the year, whereas the peninsular rivers like the Godavari, the Krishna and the Kaveri depend mainly on monsoon rainfall.

The climate of India is described as a tropical monsoon climate. The south-west monsoon brings rain from June to September and is the main source of water for agriculture. The retreating monsoon gives rain to the eastern coast, especially Tamil Nadu. Rainfall varies from the heaviest in Mawsynram and Cherrapunji in Meghalaya to the driest in western Rajasthan.
